input.rationale: Article 16 contains mutual indemnities, but Array's indemnity at 16.2 is limited to Array's own commercialization in the Array Territory, Array-sponsored Clinical Studies and breach of Article 15. There is no Vendor indemnity anywhere for Third Party intellectual property infringement — Section 11.4 instead leaves each Subject Party to defend Infringement Actions "at its own expense" — and no express duty to defend, no cover for Array's breach of Law, unauthorized disclosure of our Confidential Information or Array's gross negligence/willful misconduct. Absence of a Vendor IP indemnity is walk-away territory, so the fallback is not met. Ono's indemnity at 16.1 is also far broader than the narrow Customer indemnity the playbook permits. The procedure at 16.3 already supplies notice, sole control of the defence and full cooperation, so we add only the missing preferred heads: a stand-alone IP infringement indemnity at new 16.2A expressed to override Section 11.4, the defence duty and heads (e)-(g) in 16.2, and a narrowed 16.1. We can restore the reciprocal product-liability and clinical-study allocation if Array grants the IP indemnity.

proposal.summary: Add Array defence duty, express IP infringement indemnity and law/confidentiality/GN-WM heads; narrow Ono's indemnity
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Array's indemnity omits any third party intellectual property infringement indemnity, so we have added an express one that overrides the "own expense" defence allocation in Section 11.4, together with a duty to defend and cover for Array's breach of Law, unauthorized disclosure of our Confidential Information and Array's gross negligence or willful misconduct. In exchange we have narrowed Ono's indemnity to Ono-supplied materials and Ono's breach of Law, deleting its product-liability and Article 15 prongs; we can restore the reciprocal product-liability and clinical-study allocation if Array accepts the IP indemnity.
